construct: a COINCIDENT INSET RING pseudo — ::after at inset 0, transparent fill, uniform 1px border, host radius — whose ring COLOUR is a product of TWO enum axes while its four side WIDTHS are uniform across every combo (fluent Badge's `root::after`)
why: This is how a whole library spells its outline/tint ring: the host element carries border-width 0 and the ring lives on a coincident pseudo. The decor grammar factors a pseudo's paint uniform-or-ONE-enum-axis, so a two-axis ring colour refuses the WHOLE box (pseudo-decor-paint-multiaxis) and throws away FOUR UNIFORM FACTS (1px on all four sides, every combo) to avoid guessing the one varying one. Fusion already carries the varying half on the HOST (border-{side}-color per axis product), so the contract ships a border COLOUR with no width anywhere and core/emit-figma-script.ts's hasWidthSource correctly refuses to invent one — outline and tint mint identical to filled. fluent.badge is the measured row.
expectWhere: anatomy.root.literals.border-top-width (the ring's uniform side widths folded onto the coincident host, whose border-{side}-color the contract already carries)

canvas.note: the host node draws a 1px Figma stroke painted by its own border-{side}-color binding — the ring is the host's stroke, not a second node
